To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cigarette smoke can affect mast cell development by suppressing the surface expression of the c-kit and FcgRI receptors.
cigarette smoke medium (a complex mixture of cigarette smoke components) suppresses the development and the function of mast cells.
Cigarette smoke medium (CSm) can suppress the surface expression of FcεRI and c-kit receptors and can suppress the degranulation and cytokine release of mast cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of cigarette smoke on mast cells and the potential role of these cells in cigarette smoke-related diseases.
the effects of CSM on bone-marrow-derived-mast cells.
the role of mast cells in allergic airway diseases and the effects of cigarette smoke on the development and function of mast cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CSM exposure suppresses the surface expression of FcεRI and c-kit receptors on bone marrow-derived mast cells and thereby reduces their ability to respond to allergic stimulation.
CSM may have a negative effect on mast cell development and function, which may have an impact on the development of allergic diseases and COPD.
CSM exposure suppresses mast cell maturation and function in a TLR-independent fashion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mast cell development is suppressed and their subsequent function altered by CSM exposure.
CSM may have a direct inhibitory effect on mast cell development and activation, and that these changes may be important in the development and pathogenesis of COPD.
cigarette smoke may suppress mast cell maturation and function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CSM exposure during mast cell development may affect the function of these cells in allergic responses and that the effects of CSM are not due to LPS.
cigarette smoke may affect the development and maturation of bone-marrow derived mast cells.
mast cells are not only important in allergic diseases but also in the pathogenesis of COPD.
